title: Staged Control-Plane Upgrade Flow for Closed VPCs — Acceptance Criteria & Networking Constraints
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Short PRD defining an incremental control-plane upgrade contract for fully isolated VPC/private deployments. Goal: enable safe operator and control-plane component upgrades when customer clusters have minimal or zero egress and rely on staged mirrors or air-gapped artifact distribution. This doc prescribes networking constraints, artifact validation, canary gating, rollback criteria, and operator modes required for a non-disruptive upgrade path.
problem_statement: Customers in highly regulated environments run Redwood Private inside closed VPCs with strict egress policies or physical-media provisioning. Current upgrade paths assume intermittent internet access for image pulls and control-plane traffic which is incompatible with zero-egress installations. We need a deterministic, testable upgrade contract that operators and the on-prem agent can follow without requiring expanded network permissions.
success_metrics: 1) 99% of in-scope private upgrades complete without operator intervention under staged-mirror mode. 2) Mean time to rollback <= 20 minutes when canary fails. 3) No increase in customer-facing error-rate beyond 0.5% during upgrades. 4) Zero undocumented manual steps in runbook.
scope: In-scope: operator-controlled staged upgrade flow, image checksum orchestration, split-horizon DNS/timebound mirror windows, canary cohort selection, automated rollback triggers, telemetry hooks. Out-of-scope: full redesign of on-prem installer and custom physical-media courier services.
assumptions: 1) Customer provides at least one artifact-mirror endpoint reachable from control-plane and nodes. 2) KMS/HSM rotations are managed outside this flow. 3) Mirror signing keys are provisioned and trust chain established prior to upgrade.
constraints: - No new permanent egress requirements for customer clusters. - Upgrade must tolerate up to 30% node churn in canary cohort. - Mirror windows must be schedulable within customer maintenance windows.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Off-network artifact validation — Upgrade may proceed only when artifact checksums match signed release manifest stored on local mirror. Proof: a signed manifest AND checksum verification log present in operator audit trail.

AC-2: Split-horizon DNS fallback — During staged rollout, DNS resolution for image registry must be configurable to point to local mirror with a defined TTL and able to revert to internal registry on rollback.

AC-3: Canary cohort gating — A canary cohort (configurable by percentage or node labels) must demonstrate health (pod readiness, latency, token-level errors) for N minutes (configurable default 10m) before wider rollout.
AC-4: Time-bounded mirror window — Mirror syncs are scheduled as discrete, auditable windows; operator must detect incomplete mirror sync and halt rollout.
AC-5: Rollback automation — Failure thresholds (e.g., 5% request error-rate increase or control-plane restarts > 2 within 5m) automatically trigger rollback to previous image and postmortem creation.
AC-6: Offline bootstrap fallback — If mirror unavailable, operator must support a physical-media installation path with checksum verification and idempotent re-apply behavior.

AC-7: Telemetry & observability — Upgrade events (start, canary-pass/fail, mirror-status, rollback) must emit structured events to the control plane audit log and an on-prem telemetry sink; sample retention and schemas documented.

AC-8: Security posture preserved — The upgrade flow must not widen existing network policies; default behavior is 'fail-closed' for missing mirrors unless explicitly configured allow-fallback-to-egress=true by customer.
AC-9: Operator auditability — All decisions and automated actions must be correlated with operator identity and recorded with timestamps in audit logs for at least 90 days.
rollout_plan: 1) Development: implement operator feature flags + safe defaults. 2) Internal dogfood: deploy to 3 internal closed VPCs with synthetic mirror. 3) Beta: invite 2 existing enterprise customers on isolated clusters. 4) GA: release with runbook, console UI toggles for mirror windows and canary cohorts. Rollout controlled via private-2026.04 train.
test_plan: End-to-end mirror sync simulation (success, partial, failure)
Canary failure injection (service latency, pod OOM, K8s node drain)
Chaos test: intermittent mirror availability during rollout
monitoring_and_alerting: Define SLOs for upgrade success rate and set alerts for mirror-sync failures, canary failures, and rollback occurrences. Dashboards: Upgrade Runbook view (canary status, mirror health), per-cluster recent upgrade timeline, and token-level error trending during upgrade windows.
